operations: Bathopele is a mechanised bord-and-pillar UG2 shaft (two decline clusters to ~500 m) in Sibanye-Stillwater's Rustenburg operation, east of Rustenburg and Kroondal. Ownership changed: Anglo American Platinum sold the Rustenburg operation (incl. Bathopele) to Sibanye on 1 Nov 2016; Anglo American Platinum was renamed Valterra Platinum in 2025 and now only tolls Rustenburg concentrate. The DMPR North West row still lists the owner as Anglo American Platinum. Current operator's people (Sibanye) recorded; Valterra execs attached as group-level for re-homing.
scale_note: Rustenburg operation: 16,570 permanent employees (Dec 2025); Q1 2025 Rustenburg output 199,591 4Eoz; Bathopele Q1 2025 output down 2,970 4Eoz (7%) as the shaft approaches end of reserve life (~2028). Bulk power from the Eskom grid; no solar or renewable PPA disclosed for Rustenburg in the FY2025 20-F. Kwezi shaft restructure (1,114 jobs) announced Sept 2026.

operations: Marula Platinum (Pty) Ltd: 73% Implats, 27% BEE (Marula Community Trust, Tubatse Platinum, Mmakau Mining, Marula ESOT). ~35 km north-west of Burgersfort on farms Winnaarshoek, Clapham, Driekop and Forest Hill (eastern limb). Two decline shaft systems (Driekop, Clapham) and a concentrator; concentrate trucked to Impala Rustenburg under a life-of-mine IRS offtake. Makgomo Chrome JV recovers chrome from tailings. No ownership change.
scale_note: FY2023: 1.935 Mt milled, 241 koz 6E in concentrate, 3,922 own employees + 1,032 contractors (Marula fact sheet, Jan 2024). No site renewable PPA disclosed.

operations: DMPR Gauteng list row 'Elandsfontein Chrome Mine - Northam Platinum - Chromite/PGM - Underground - Ekurhuleni' is mislocated: Northam has no operation in Gauteng. It is Northam's Eland mine on farm Elandsfontein 440 JQ, 12 km east of Brits at Mooinooi, Madibeng, North West - the same operation as the DMPR North West row 'Mooinooi Platinum Mine' (record o_mu8ko0n6_7b7mi). See that record for operations, scale and energy.
scale_note: See o_mu8ko0n6_7b7mi (Eland): F2026 308,831 t chrome concentrate and 91,205 oz 4E; 20 MW solar + 40 MWh BESS under construction.
status_flag: duplicate-of-existing-record - Northam Platinum — Mooinooi Platinum Mine

operations: Northam's Eland mine (Eland Platinum (Pty) Ltd, 100% Northam Platinum Holdings), on farm Elandsfontein 440 JQ at Mooinooi, 12 km east of Brits, Madibeng, North West. Shallow hybrid UG2 underground operation via three interconnected declines (Kukama, Nyala, Maroelabult), concentrator and expanded chrome recovery circuit (commissioned Dec 2025). Acquired from Glencore Dec 2017; Maroelabult added from Eastern Platinum 2022. Separate from Zondereinde (not a duplicate of that record). Same operation as DMPR Gauteng row 'Elandsfontein Chrome Mine' (o_mu8ko0n6_5vuys).
scale_note: F2026 (to 30 Jun 2026): 91,205 oz 4E in concentrate (+25.9%) and 308,831 t chrome concentrate (+49.5%), ~60% of steady state; 50 stoping crews; target 150 koz/y 4E by 2029 and >2,500 direct jobs at steady state; F2026 capex R1.4bn. Energy: 20 MW solar (to grow to 40 MW) with 40 MWh battery under construction at Eland (site clearing Aug 2026), wheeled across Northam operations under an Eskom wheeling agreement; Northam says Eland is to be the first SA PGM mine run solely on renewables (Vision 2031).

commodity: Ferrochrome / chrome (smelting; chrome recovery from Marikana UG2 tailings)
operations: DMPR row 'Wonderkop Chrome Mine - Glencore-Merafe - Surface & Processing - Madibeng' is the Glencore-Merafe Chrome Venture's Wonderkop ferrochrome smelter at Wonderkop/Marikana plus the Marikana chrome recovery plants that treat Sibanye-Stillwater's Marikana UG2 tailings under the 2011 Marikana Contract (enhanced and extended from 1 Nov 2025, with the Venture also taking over management of Sibanye's Kroondal and Rustenburg CRPs). It is a smelter/processing site, not a mine; the Venture's mines are Helena, Magareng, Thorncliffe (eastern limb) and Waterval, Kroondal (Rustenburg). Venture: Glencore 79.5% / Merafe Resources 20.5%. Wonderkop smelting suspended 31 May 2025 and placed on care and maintenance (Glencore-Merafe statement 18 Nov 2025); restart announced 26 Jun 2026 after an Eskom NPA at 62c/kWh; ramp-up to complete by end-2026.
scale_note: Wonderkop smelter: six furnaces, design capacity 553 kt/y ferrochrome (Merafe 2016 site visit); Venture ~2.3 Mt/y ferrochrome capacity, 301 kt produced in 2024 (curtailed). Energy: Eskom Negotiated Pricing Agreement at 62c/kWh, three-year framework, Nersa-approved 29 May 2026; up to 1,500 jobs were at risk in the 2025-26 S189. No renewable PPA disclosed.
status_flag: doubtful - restarting from care-and-maintenance (Jun 2026 Eskom NPA), ramp-up to end-2026; site is a smelter and chrome recovery plant, not a mine

operations: Samancor Chrome's Eastern Chrome Mines (ECM): three underground mines, two opencast mines, four surface beneficiation plants and four tailings re-treatment plants along ~100 km of the eastern limb in the Steelpoort valley (~350 km from Johannesburg), feeding Samancor's Tubatse Ferrochrome and Tubatse Alloy smelters at Steelpoort. Samancor Chrome is privately held (head office Sandton). No ownership change.
scale_note: No ECM tonnage or headcount published on samancorcr.com. Energy: Samancor Chrome's smelters obtained an Eskom tariff of 62c/kWh (Eskom, 10 Apr 2026; up to five-year NPA), cancelled its S189 and said production would resume within six months (Jun 2026). Head office switchboard +27 11 245-1000.

operations: The DMPR Mpumalanga row 'Steelpoort Valley Mines - Samancor / Glencore / Assore Consortium - Chrome - Underground & Surface - Steelpoort' is an aggregate placeholder, not an operation: no such consortium exists. The Steelpoort valley chrome mines belong to three separate owners - Samancor Eastern Chrome Mines (already on file as o_mu8ko0n6_qr2xm), the Glencore-Merafe Chrome Venture's Eastern Chrome Mines (Helena, Magareng, Thorncliffe) and Assore's Dwarsrivier Chrome Mine - and all are in Limpopo (Sekhukhune), not Mpumalanga. Recommend deleting this record and, if wanted, creating separate records for Glencore-Merafe Eastern Chrome Mines and Assore Dwarsrivier.
status_flag: doubtful - aggregate DMPR row; Samancor part duplicates 'Samancor Eastern Chrome Mines'; Glencore-Merafe Eastern Chrome Mines and Assore Dwarsrivier are separate operations not on file

operations: Bushveld Vametco Alloys (Pty) Ltd: integrated open-pit magnetite mine and salt-roast/leach vanadium plant on farms Uitvalgrond 431 JQ and Krokodilkraal 426 JQ, ~8-10 km north-east of Brits, Madibeng, North West - NOT Bela-Bela, Limpopo as the DMPR Limpopo row states. Bushveld Vametco Holdings, Bushveld Vametco Alloys and Bushveld Minerals SA entered business rescue in Nov 2024 (joint BRPs Piers Marsden and Jenna Osborne, Matuson & Associates); plant shut Dec 2024 - Apr 2025; business rescue plans published 17 Jun 2025 and adopted 25 Jun 2025 (accelerated sale of the Vametco business to a preferred bidder, then receivership); Bushveld Minerals SA finally wound up by court order 18 Aug 2026; Guernsey parent Bushveld Minerals Ltd in liquidation. Vametco Alloys still in business rescue per the July 2026 BRP update; purchaser not yet public.
scale_note: Nameplate ~3,000 t vanadium/y (miningdataonline); JORC resource 181.5 Mt, reserves 46.2 Mt (Bushveld). Energy: 3.5 MW solar PV + 1 MW/4 MWh vanadium redox flow battery mini-grid at Vametco, built by Bushveld Energy as an IPP selling to the mine (SANEA Power Project of the Year 2022; scheduled H1 2023).
status_flag: doubtful - in business rescue since Nov 2024, plant idle since Dec 2024, being sold under the adopted BR plan; purchaser not yet public

commodity: Nickel (with copper, cobalt, PGM; chrome from stockpiles)
operations: ARM's Nkomati Nickel mine on the Uitkomst Complex between Machadodorp (eNtokozweni), Waterval Boven and Badplaas, Mpumalanga - NOT Rustenburg, North West as the DMPR North West row 'Nkomati Nickel Operations (NW Portion)' (status 'Limited / Joint Operations') states; there is no North West portion. Ownership changed: Nornickel's 50% sold to ARM, completed Jul 2025, so ARM is 100% owner. Underground on care and maintenance from 2015; open-pit mining ceased Feb 2021; whole mine on care and maintenance since 2021; chrome-washing plant recommissioned 2025 for stockpiles. ARM board approved an open-pit restart on 23 Jul 2026 (R753m capex; plant refurbishment from Jul 2026, mining from Oct 2026; 13-year LoM) backed by a conditional nickel-concentrate offtake with Boliden (Harjavalta), Apr 2026.
scale_note: Restart steady state 56,000 t/y nickel concentrate; NPV R764m, IRR 28%. No renewable PPA disclosed.

commodity: Heavy mineral sands (ilmenite, rutile, zircon, leucoxene)
operations: Undeveloped project on the Wild Coast between the Mzamba and Mtentu rivers, Amadiba area near Xolobeni, Mbizana (Winnie Madikizela-Mandela LM). Held by Transworld Energy and Resources (SA) (Pty) Ltd (TEM): 56% Mineral Commodities Ltd (MRC, Australia) with BEE partner Keysha Investments 178; MRC agreed in 2016 to divest its 56% to Keysha but the sale never completed. Mining right granted Jul 2008, revoked May 2011; 2015 re-application frozen by a ministerial moratorium; Nov 2018 High Court ruling requires community consent (Amadiba Crisis Committee opposition, ongoing). MRC entered voluntary administration 18 Dec 2025 and was delisted from the ASX 18 Jun 2026 - there is no active corporate counterparty; the MRC board page (Brian Moller, Independent Non-Executive Chairman; Zamile David Qunya, Non-Executive Director, et al.) is stale.
scale_note: Resource 346 Mt at 5% total heavy minerals (MRC). Has never operated; no employees, no power demand.
